---
title: "6. Verify and explain: Your own study"
---

## Verify one sample

Run from the main folder; replace SAMPLE_ID with an actual ID:

```bash
Rscript scripts/R/verify_sample.R data/my-study results/my-study config/my-study.tsv SAMPLE_ID
```

All three rows should show TRUE. The verifier checks current input bytes,
count total, observed features and Shannon. Agreement checks arithmetic; it
does not validate sequencing quality, sample identity or every model estimate.

## Explain the exploration

Write one sentence per figure. For composition, compare named OTUs and
acknowledge the pooled remainder. For Shannon and richness, check sample
values and group summaries. For PCoA, name the distance and axis percentages;
check whether the pattern persists in the depth sensitivity. For the heatmap
and prevalence plot, distinguish high abundance from frequent detection.

## Explain the tests

Record the group term's R-squared and p-value in `permanova.tsv`, the
covariates in `model-matrix.tsv`, and dispersion results. Compare the two
distance definitions without choosing a favourite p-value. Dispersion is not
adjusted for the covariates in the PERMANOVA model.

If differential abundance was run, select an OTU in
`differential-abundance.tsv`. Check its full ID, contrast direction, natural-log
effect, standard error, adjusted p-value and sensitivity flag. Recalculate
exp(effect) for its model-estimated fold change. Locate it in the full
relative-abundance table to understand the unadjusted display; the two values
answer different questions.

An empty discoveries table is a valid outcome. Explain insufficient evidence
under the model, rather than claiming identical communities or changing the
threshold to obtain hits.

**Human → AI → Human task:** write your result paragraph first. Give AI the
relevant figures, exact table rows, model and contrast. Ask it to identify
unsupported numbers, reversed effects and causal wording. Accept changes
only after checking them yourself. Finish with one limitation and a useful
next scientific question.
